rows.verified: A confined space is enclosed or largely enclosed and presents a reasonably foreseeable specified risk to workers.
Specified confined-space risks include fire, explosion, loss of consciousness, asphyxiation and drowning.
Work in confined spaces should be avoided wherever possible.
If entry is unavoidable, the particular confined-space risks must be assessed and a safe system of work planned.
Where harmful fumes may be present, ventilation or removal of the fumes must be considered.
Where liquids or gases could flood the space, isolation such as locking valves shut should be considered.
If oxygen is insufficient, suitable breathing apparatus or ventilation must be provided before entry.
Adequate emergency arrangements are required and rescue planning must not rely only on the emergency services.
Confined-space controls depend on geometry, atmosphere, process residues, isolations, ingress routes, work activity, entrants and rescue capability.
Confined-space evidence is space-, task-, atmosphere- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fatality or injury probability.
Work at height remains one of the biggest causes of workplace fatalities and major injuries.
Work at height includes any place where a person could fall a distance liable to cause personal injury if precautions were absent.
Work at height must be properly planned before it is carried out.
Work at height must be appropriately supervised and carried out by competent people.
The right type of equipment must be selected for the work at height.
Employers and those controlling work at height must assess the risks first.
Risks from working on or near fragile surfaces must be properly managed.
Equipment used for work at height must be properly inspected and maintained.
Work-at-height controls depend on fall distance, edges, openings, fragile surfaces, access, weather, equipment, supervision and rescue planning.
Work-at-height evidence is task-, location-, equipment- and condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fall probability.
